# PDF import fixture

The `test_pdf_import` suite's fixture PDF is **not** a checked-in file: it is
embedded as base64 in `tests/test_pdf_import.cpp` (`kFixturePdfB64`). This
directory exists to document its provenance and regeneration.

## What the fixture exercises

A single page (base-14 Helvetica family + Courier, no embedded fonts) that
drives every pdf2md.js heuristic end-to-end through the real
`PdfImporter::convert()` path:

- ATX headings via font-size deltas (24 pt title, 14 pt section vs 12 pt body)
- body paragraphs
- italic emphasis (`Helvetica-Oblique`)
- a two-line Courier monospace code block
- bullet (`\267`) and ordered lists
- a 2-column × 3-row pipe table (aligned x-starts at 80 / 240)
- a cross-line hard-hyphen wrap (rejoined by de-hyphenation)
- a lone "Page 1" footer

## How it is produced

Hand-authored PDF content streams (boring `BT`/`ET` text blocks), generated by
`tests/gen_pdf_fixture.py`. It is deliberately not generated via the app's own
PDF export, so the test never depends on another subsystem.

## Regenerating

```bash
tests/gen_pdf_fixture.py               # print base64 (one line)
tests/gen_pdf_fixture.py --verify      # check against kFixturePdfB64 in the test
```

If the fixture must change: edit `TEXT_LINES` in `tests/gen_pdf_fixture.py`,
then paste the new base64 into `kFixturePdfB64` in
`tests/test_pdf_import.cpp`. `--verify` must pass.

## Repeated header/footer strip

The fixture is a single page, so `stripHeaderFooter` (which needs repetition
across pages) is not exercised by it. That behavior is covered instead by the
synthetic heuristic test `PdfImporterHeuristics.RepeatedHeaderFooterStrippedAcrossPages`,
which feeds multi-page `getTextContent()`-shaped JSON directly to pdf2md.js.
